Maya — thanks for the note. Quick summary up front: we support a two-phase decommission: 1) operational cutover + escrow/backup verification, 2) final cryptographic zeroize and operator deprovisioning. For ACME we recommend a staged finalization so your apps have a rollback window.

High-level checklist (attached as hsm_decommission_checklist.pdf):
- Pre-check: confirm active sessions, KV cache flush, and snapshot of running models that reference keys.
- Escrow: create encrypted escrow bundle, store in customer-controlled storage (you keep the key to unwrap).
- Audit snapshot: capture signed auditchain snapshot (SHA256 hashes) and publish to an immutable store.
- Operator ceremony: require at least two named operator sign-offs; we capture signatures and 2FA assertion tokens.
- Grace window: 48–72 hours for rollback before final zeroize.
- Final zeroize: HSM zeroize command, verification of zeroed key slots, and release of final signed zeroize event.

Audit retention: we provide the signed auditchain record (log bundle with RFC3339 timestamps and a signed hash). Redwood retains operational logs for 90 days by default; for decommission evidence we produce a signed artifact that you can store indefinitely. If you need Redwood to retain copies longer, that is a procurement add-on we can schedule.

I'll loop in Kim and Ben for the operator-authz specifics and the template for sign-off that procurement can feed to legal. Attaching the checklist and a template for operator authorization.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: Operator authorization model & auditchain details

Maya / Jasmine / Ben — adding the authorization details you asked for. Two points to highlight that differ from a standard key rotation:

1) Operator authz model:
- We require enumerated operator roles in the ceremony (Operator-A, Operator-B) with unique identities tied to our SSO and an HSM-managed CSR for signing.
- During the pre-decommission window we create a short-lived PKI leaf for the ceremony that is stamped by our CA and pinned to the auditchain event.
- Each operator signs the ceremony transcript; signatures include a timestamp and a 2FA OTP confirmation.

2) Auditchain & immutable evidence:
- We produce an append-only auditchain file: newline-delimited JSON events with event IDs and SHA256 chaining. Each event is signed using our ops-key and the final chain root is notarized with an attestation from the HSM (attestation cert attached as part of the audit bundle).
- The auditbundle contains the evidence package: auditchain-sample.log, operator attestations, and a PDF of the ceremony transcript. For privacy we redact session tokens and only include event metadata and event hashes.

Retention & tamper-evidence:
- The auditbundle contains the chain root and a PKCS7 signature. You can verify the chain locally; we can also publish the chain root to an ACME-owned S3 bucket if you prefer out-of-band verification.
- If you request, SecureOps can independently verify the chain before final zeroize.

Operational request for procurement:
- Confirm the canonical ACME contact who will receive the signed artifact and where (S3 bucket + email).
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to hold escrow copies for 30/90/365 days.

— Kim
Kimberly Park
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Maya / team — quick operational commitments from Redwood before you lock the change board:
- Non-repudiable revocation: yes. We will produce a signed Revocation Assertion (PDF with PKCS7 signature) once HSM zeroize completes; that artifact will reference the auditchain root and include operator cert fingerprints.
- Escrow encryption: please send the wrapping public key (PEM) to secure-escrow@redwood.ai; we'll generate the bundle, encrypt with your key, and include the encryption metadata in the signed artifact.
- Independent verification: SecureOps is on-board; we will schedule a 1-hour live session during the grace window (we'll allocate two operators and one engineering observer).
- Timeline: proposed cutover Fri Nov 26 22:00–23:00 PST, 48-hour rollback window, final zeroize Sun Nov 28 22:00 PST unless ACME requests earlier finalization.

Action items for ACME: send wrapping key PEM, confirm recipient S3 bucket, authorize DocuSign envelope (linked), and confirm SecureOps scope. Once we have that we will publish the DocuSign and sign-off template for authorized operators.
